# Domain and application code

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_agent_rules.py from rules.yml; do not edit by hand. Implements AGT-010, AGT-011. Only rules that no CI job or linter enforces. -->

- LLM calls, prompt assembly and output parsing MUST NOT appear in `domain/`; a business rule that can be written as deterministic code MUST be written as deterministic code in `domain/` (see 04-engineering-principles.md) (ARC-014).
- Dependency injection SHOULD be by constructor or function parameter against a Protocol; global singletons and module-level clients SHOULD NOT be used (ARC-010).
- Names MUST state intent in domain language (`PremiumQuote`, `is_eligible_for_waiver`), functions MUST be verbs or questions, and the same concept MUST have the same name everywhere (CLN-010).
- Names SHOULD describe domain concepts, not technology (`ClaimRepository`, not `SqlHelper`), and SHOULD NOT use `utils`, `helpers`, `manager` or `misc` (STR-019).
- Domain values SHOULD be immutable (frozen dataclasses or frozen models); module-level mutable state MUST NOT be used, and `global` MUST NOT appear (`PLW0603` is in the selected `PL` set) (CLN-008).
- Failure MUST be signalled by raising a specific domain exception (defined in `domain/errors.py` or `application`); functions MUST NOT return `None`, `-1`, empty strings or `False` to mean "something went wrong" (CLN-019).
- A function SHOULD do one thing, read top to bottom, and use early returns and guard clauses instead of nesting beyond three levels (CLN-005).
- A regulatory or business-rule comment MUST cite the rule source by identifier or document name so a reviewer can check it; MUST NOT invent a citation (CLN-031).
- Money is integer cents, never floats; add Hypothesis property tests for invariants (TST-020).
